newsitem.title: USA: Republicans call for new simple tax system.
newsitem.headline: Republicans call for new simple tax system.

text.p: Republicans want to abolish the current federal income tax system and replace it with one that is simple and fair, House Majority Leader Dick Armey of Texas said Saturday.
"We need to scrap our current income tax system and start over from stratch," Armey said in the Republican response to President Clinton's weekly radio address.
He said a poll released Friday found 55 percent of taxpayers needed help in preparing their taxes by the April 15 filing date because the system was so complex.
The poll was conducted for Armey by Luntz Research Companies of Arlington, Va., among 900 adults and had a margin of error of plus or minus 3.3 percent.

"That poll released yesterday showed that 70 percent of Americans believe we need to fundamentally overhaul our tax system and replace it with something new. Not just tinkering around the edges, or fiddling with the details. We need a whole new tax system, one that's simple, honest, direct and fair," Armey said.
He said Clinton's proposals for management changes at the Internal Revenue Service were not good enough.

"Republicans in Congress are determined to replace the current tax code with a tax system that is simplier, fairer and less of a burden on American families. We must reduce the family tax burden to give parents the freedom to meet their responsibilities to their children."

House Republicans have scheduled a vote next Tuesday on a proposed constitutional amendment to require a two-thirds majority vote in both the House and Senate to raise taxes. The amendment has also been introduced in the Senate and needs a two-thirds majority in both chambers to pass.
Armey and Republican Sen. Richard Shelby of Alabama last month proposed replacing the graduated income tax system with a flat tax of 17 percent of income with all deductions and credits eliminated.
Republicans also want to eliminate federal taxes on capital gains and estates but the administration is opposed because of fears that the loss of revenue will increase the budget deficit.
